title: Decode an instruction
description:
In the tiny computer of lesson 4.04 each instruction is one number: the hundreds digit is the operation, the rest is an address. Write:

```python
def decode(code)                 # 110 -> ("LOAD", 10), 605 -> ("JUMPZ", 5), 0 -> ("HALT", 0)
def encode(name, address)        # ("STORE", 12) -> 412
```

| Hundreds digit | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operation | HALT | LOAD | ADD | SUB | STORE | JUMP | JUMPZ |

For a hundreds digit with no operation (7, 8 or 9), `decode` returns `("???", address)`.

`NAMES = ["HALT", "LOAD", "ADD", "SUB", "STORE", "JUMP", "JUMPZ"]` makes both directions short: `NAMES[1]` is `"LOAD"`, `NAMES.index("LOAD")` is 1.
